speaker: Doctor
text: I apologize for the confusion in my previous assessment. To properly evaluate your persistent bleeding and easy bruising, I need to start fresh. Can you tell me if you have a personal or family history of bleeding disorders, such as hemophilia or von Willebrand disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience swelling or pain in your joints after minor injuries or without any known trauma? Have you noticed excessive bleeding from other sites, such as your nose or during circumcision?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of joint swelling and easy bruising, I suspect a factor deficiency. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_Panel (PT, aPTT, FVIII, FIX).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Prothrombin Time: 15 sec, Partial Thromboplastin Time: 60 sec, Fibrin Split Products: Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged aPTT with a normal PT strongly suggests Hemophilia A or B. REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_Level, Factor_IX_Level.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal factor levels but prolonged aPTT and family history, I suspect von Willebrand disease. REQUEST TEST: Von_Willebrand_Factor_Antigen, Ristocetin_Cofactor_Activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since standard factor assays are normal but the aPTT is prolonged, I suspect an inhibitor or a rare factor deficiency like Factor XI. REQUEST TEST: Factor_XI_Level, Lupus_Anticoagulant.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Factor XI Level: Normal, Lupus Anticoagulant: Negative

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the standard coagulation factors and von Willebrand disease tests are normal, I need to evaluate platelet function. Do you have a history of frequent nosebleeds, heavy menstrual bleeding (if applicable), or bleeding from minor cuts that lasts longer than usual?

REQUEST TEST: Platelet_Count, Bleeding_Time, Platelet_Aggregation_Studies

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet Count: 160,000/mm3, Bleeding Time: 6 min, Platelet Aggregation Studies: Abnormal (defective aggregation with ristocetin, normal with ADP, collagen, and epinephrine)

speaker: Doctor
text: The abnormal platelet aggregation with ristocetin but normal response to other agonists is diagnostic for Bernard-Soulier syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Bernard-Soulier syndrome
